data.title: British Columbia
data.summary: A fourteen-night journey blending Western Canada's vibrant iconic hubs such as Vancouver, Victoria, Whistler, and the Okanagan Valley, with pristine lakes, coastal wild, and alpine communities.
data.description: We will explore British Columbia over 14 nights and 13 days, starting with 4 nights in Vancouver to experience coastal urban life, the mountains of Whistler, and the breathtaking landscapes of Vancouver Island. Afterwards, we’ll dive into the Okanagan Valley, one of Canada’s top wine regions, spending 10 nights based in the city of Kelowna, the heart of the valley. Each day, the journey opens up to the region in a different way: the majesty of the Pacific Ocean, the Sea-to-Sky alpine route, the British charm of Victoria, biking through Myra Canyon across historic suspended trestles, wine tastings with spectacular panoramic views, a boat ride on Okanagan Lake, and gentle hikes along vibrant, color-shifting lakes. A niche experience away from the crowded tourist routes, designed to leave you with memories that truly last.
data.territory: British Columbia is a province of striking contrasts: from the coastal metropolis of Vancouver surrounded by sea and mountains, the majestic alpine route to Whistler, and the island beauty of Victoria (Vancouver Island), to the fertile, warm Okanagan Valley with hundreds of vineyards and wineries dotted along the lake and its surrounding hills.
data.audience: A trip designed for adults seeking authentic places, a sustainable pace, and a shared experience built with intention and care.
data.climate: In Vancouver, Victoria, and Whistler, the coastal and alpine summer is cool and mild: 18–24 °C (64–75 °F). In Kelowna, Lake Country, Vernon, and Osoyoos, the climate is warmer and drier: 25–35 °C (77–95 °F).

paidOnArrival.note: Transport operating fund: €150 per person, paid in cash on arrival. It covers verifiable shared expenses: gas, parking, tolls.

team.name: Federica Caglioti
team.bio: Art Director and founder of Studio Superbo, with an international creative career. She hosts this Off The Map trip and sets its rhythm, shaping an experience that puts together local culture, places with a real connection to nature, and moments that stay in your memory rather than only your phone's.

team.name: Nora Maria Loya Ledesma
team.bio: A chef with more than fifteen years across Spain, the United States, Mexico and Canada. She cooks this edition of Off The Map, with global influences and local ingredients, and curates the food experiences of the region — including a guide to local options for the meals that are on your own.

blocks.title: Stanley Park
blocks.description: Bike ride or walk through Stanley Park along the Seawall, a world-famous 1,000-acre urban park surrounded by ocean waters, ancient cedar trees, and indigenous Totem Poles with views of Burrard Inlet.

blocks.title: Lunch at Granville Island
blocks.description: Free time at Granville Island Public Market, a buzzing waterfront cultural hub filled with artisanal food stalls, fresh seafood, local cheeses, and craft bakeries.

blocks.title: English Bay
blocks.description: Walking tour along English Bay waterfront (a popular sandy beach promenade facing the open ocean) with free time to browse local boutiques along Robson Street or West 4th.

blocks.title: Dinner
blocks.description: Dinner prepared by the chef.

blocks.title: Breakfast

blocks.title: Ferry to Vancouver Island
blocks.description: Departure to Tsawwassen. Catch the BC Ferry across the Georgia Strait (1.5-hour scenic crossing navigating through the quiet channels of the Gulf Islands).

blocks.title: Victoria
blocks.description: Tour of BC's capital at the Inner Harbour, featuring the grand neoclassical BC Parliament Buildings and the historic Fairmont Empress Hotel (built in 1908).

blocks.title: Lunch
blocks.description: Free time at Victoria's Inner Harbour.

blocks.title: Butchart Gardens
blocks.description: Stroll through 55 acres of world-renowned botanical displays, including the dramatic Sunken Garden, Japanese Garden, and Rose Garden. Visit duration approx. 2-3 hours.

blocks.title: Ferry back
blocks.description: Return ferry to Vancouver.

blocks.title: Dinner
blocks.description: Prepared by the chef.

blocks.title: Breakfast
blocks.description: Breakfast and briefing.

blocks.title: Sea-to-Sky Highway
blocks.description: Iconic drive (Highway 99) skimming the dramatic fjord walls of Howe Sound, with a photo stop at Shannon Falls (a towering 335-meter waterfall tumbling over granite cliffs).

blocks.title: Whistler Village
blocks.description: Pedestrian-only alpine village at the base of Whistler and Blackcomb mountains. Time to take the Peak 2 Peak Gondola (a record-breaking cable car spanning between two mountain peaks) or hike accessible alpine trails.

blocks.title: Lunch
blocks.description: Free time at recommended bistros in Whistler Village.

blocks.title: Drive back
blocks.description: Coastal drive back to Vancouver in the late afternoon light.

blocks.title: Free evening
blocks.description: Free evening in Vancouver to sample the city's celebrated culinary scene (Asian cuisine, fresh seafood).

blocks.title: Breakfast
blocks.description: Breakfast and briefing.

blocks.title: Drive to Kelowna
blocks.description: Scenic 4-hour drive climbing through the Cascade Mountain passes and transitioning into the warm, pine-forested semi-arid hills of the Okanagan Valley.

blocks.title: Lunch
blocks.description: En route selection by the chef.

blocks.title: Arrival in Kelowna
blocks.description: Villa check-in, settling in, and orientation walk.

blocks.title: Dinner

blocks.title: Breakfast

blocks.title: Local art and culture
blocks.description: Departure to the Cultural District, the cultural heart of the city, and visit the Okanagan Wine & Orchard Museum. Between museums, a pause to enjoy local coffee at Sprout, a renowned bakery famous for its excellent, locally sourced products.

blocks.title: Lakeside walk
blocks.description: Walk to Kelowna City Park on the shores of Okanagan Lake.

blocks.title: Lunch on Bernard Road
blocks.description: A brief stop for a classic North American brunch on famous Bernard Road, downtown's main street.

blocks.title: Electric boat tour on Okanagan Lake
blocks.description: We board to cruise the beautiful Okanagan Lake for an hour and admire the scenery from a different perspective.

blocks.title: Free exploration
blocks.description: At the end of the boat tour, free time for a couple of hours to explore the area independently.

blocks.title: CRAFT Beer Market
blocks.description: We meet at CRAFT Beer Market Kelowna, known for its craft beer and its patio overlooking the lake.

blocks.title: Dinner
blocks.description: Prepared at home by the chef.

blocks.title: Breakfast
blocks.description: Breakfast and briefing.

blocks.title: Oyama Lookout
blocks.description: Departure to Lake Country. First stop at Oyama Lookout to enjoy a panoramic view of the area.

blocks.title: Tasting at 50th Parallel Estate Winery
blocks.description: 30-minute tasting at the renowned 50th Parallel Estate Winery, one of the most highly rated wineries in the Okanagan Valley. The visit offers insight into a contemporary winery highlighted for its wine quality and sustainable viticulture approach. The guided tasting provides an introduction to the house style and the primary characteristics of its labels.

blocks.title: Tasting at Gray Monk Estate Winery
blocks.description: One-hour tasting at the historic Gray Monk Estate Winery, one of the most representative wineries in the valley. The guided experience dives into its signature wines, with special attention to varieties grown in the region and the character of the terroir.

blocks.title: Lunch at Peak Cellars
blocks.description: Lunch at one of the restaurants overlooking the vineyards of Peak Cellars, located in the heart of Lake Country. In addition to its expressive, high-quality wines, the winery is known for its Garden Bistro's culinary offerings, featuring fresh, seasonal ingredients inspired by local traditions.

blocks.title: Kaloya Regional Park
blocks.description: After lunch, we will visit Kaloya Regional Park, a natural area overlooking the impressive Kalamalka Lake. In the late afternoon, return home.

blocks.title: Dinner
blocks.description: Dinner prepared by the chef.

blocks.title: Breakfast
blocks.description: Breakfast and briefing.

blocks.title: Bike ride in Myra Canyon
blocks.description: Departure to Myra Canyon, one of the region's most iconic spots. A bike ride of approximately 2 to 2.5 hours along the famous trestles route: historic wooden suspended bridges crossing the canyon. The route is scenic and accessible, featuring spectacular views of the valley, tunnels carved into rock, and a pace suitable for everyone.

blocks.title: Lunch
blocks.description: Lunch at one of the restaurants handpicked by the chef.

blocks.title: Free afternoon
blocks.description: The afternoon is completely free to explore Kelowna independently: lakeside walks, shopping, or personal time. You pick.

blocks.title: Pick-up and return
blocks.description: Meeting point and return home.

blocks.title: Dinner
blocks.description: Dinner at home prepared by the chef.

blocks.title: Breakfast
blocks.description: Breakfast and briefing.

blocks.title: Kangaroo Creek Farm
blocks.description: Departure. Arrival at Kangaroo Creek Farm, a unique place where we will enjoy an immersive experience connecting with rare and fascinating animals such as kangaroos, capybaras, wallabies, and other species.

blocks.title: Fruit picking
blocks.description: Transfer to a local orchard for a fruit picking experience: one of the Okanagan Valley's most authentic activities, deeply tied to the land.

blocks.title: Lunch by the lake
blocks.description: Arrival at Bertram Creek Regional Park for a picnic lunch (self-service or prepared by the chef) by the lake. A relaxed moment to eat outdoors and enjoy the scenery accompanied by local wine.

blocks.title: Summerhill Pyramid Winery
blocks.description: Summerhill is one of the area's most iconic wineries due to its pyramid-shaped architecture. Tour of the property and its outdoor grounds. Optional tasting for those who wish to delve deeper into the experience.

blocks.title: Dinner
blocks.description: Dinner prepared by the chef.

blocks.title: Breakfast
blocks.description: Breakfast and briefing.

blocks.title: Pincushion Mountain hike
blocks.description: Departure to Pincushion Mountain for a moderate hike. The perfect blend of fresh mountain air, quiet cedar paths, and top-of-the-world lake vistas experienced at a natural, comfortable pace.

blocks.title: Lunch in Peachland
blocks.description: Upon finishing the hike, we head to Bliss Bakery & Bistro for an authentically local experience.

blocks.title: Mission Hill Family Estate
blocks.description: Arrival at Mission Hill, recognized for the sixth time in recent years as Canada's top winery. Tour of the property and outdoor grounds. Optional tasting for those who wish to dive deeper into the experience.

blocks.title: Cooking class
blocks.description: Cooking session with the chef, lasting approximately 2.5 hours, focused on North American cuisine and using the fruit collected during fruit picking.

blocks.title: Dinner
blocks.description: The day concludes with dinner, sharing the dishes prepared together.

blocks.title: Breakfast
blocks.description: Breakfast and briefing.

blocks.title: Kalamalka Lake
blocks.description: Departure to Kalamalka Lake, considered by National Geographic as one of the 10 most beautiful lakes in the world, it will be our morning destination for a moderate hike.

blocks.title: Hike: Parabola, Lookout and the Wall Loop Trail
blocks.description: Approximately 7 km with spectacular views of the turquoise-hued lake, taking around 2 hours. After the hike, we will go down to the lake for a swim or a walk along the beach.

blocks.title: Lunch
blocks.description: Lunch at one of the cafes selected by the chef in Vernon.

blocks.title: Free afternoon
blocks.description: Free time to explore Vernon independently: shopping in downtown stores (30th Avenue), local art galleries, cafes, or simply relaxing.

blocks.title: BX Falls
blocks.description: We will gather to visit BX Falls, waterfalls accessible via a short hike down a picturesque wooden staircase.

blocks.title: Dinner and bowling
blocks.description: Dinner at BNA Vernon, a casual and authentic spot. Optional bowling for those interested in an evening activity.

blocks.title: Breakfast
blocks.description: Breakfast and briefing.

blocks.title: To Penticton
blocks.description: Departure to Penticton.

blocks.title: Penticton Channel float
blocks.description: We will float down the iconic Penticton Channel, the stretch of water connecting Okanagan Lake to Skaha Lake, one of the region's most beloved summer activities. Approximately a peaceful hour-long float between the two lakes.

blocks.title: Lunch
blocks.description: Lunch at a downtown Penticton restaurant selected by the chef.

blocks.title: Brewery route
blocks.description: Walking tour through the Penticton Beer Blocks, the brewery heart of the city, recognized as the Craft Beer Capital of Canada. Stop at Neighbourhood Brewing, featuring a spacious patio and outdoor fireplace, and Yellow Dog, its sister brewery within the same complex. Time to sample beer flights and discover neighboring breweries independently.

blocks.title: Free afternoon
blocks.description: Free time to explore Penticton's lakefront or relax before returning.

blocks.title: Hike

blocks.title: Lunch
